VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (Nasdaq: VRDF)
## Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders — quarter ended September 30, 2026

DRAFT — prepared by IR for review by Dana Whitcombe (CEO) and Mark Ostrander (CFO). For release with Q3 FY2026 results on Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET.

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center momentum is the story of our third quarter, and it is the engine that will carry Veridane forward. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) grew net sales 13.4% year over year, we won two new hyperscale platform awards, and our data-center backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. Total backlog ended the quarter at $918.0 million, up 13.0%, giving us visibility well into fiscal 2027. Growth is not evenly spread across our markets, but it is compounding where demand is strongest, and it is structural.

The quarter also reflected the challenges we have flagged to you: our core commercial HVAC business was soft, and our voluntary GV-400 valve recall weighed on results. Net sales were $412.6 million, adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, and adjusted EPS was $0.15. Reported results also include the recall and restructuring charges described below; the KPI table accompanying this letter presents the quarter's GAAP results in full, together with reconciliations of our non-GAAP measures. We moved fast on the recall, we have a clear and specific cost plan in Project Keystone, and we are updating our full-year guidance to reflect the demand environment we see.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale platform awards won in the quarter.
- Record data-center backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million and adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- Voluntary, proactive GV-400 recall completed with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) under its Fast Track program — root cause corrected, replacement valves shipping since September 28, and no injuries reported.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of run-rate cost savings by the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** TDC net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from $137.8 million a year ago, driven by sustained demand for our liquid-cooling portfolio across hyperscale and colocation customers. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger, launched in the second quarter with two hyperscale customers, continued to ramp, and the two new hyperscale platform awards won this quarter validate the roadmap we shared with you in August. TDC backlog finished the quarter at a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year, reflecting demand from both new and existing customers. Liquid cooling is moving from pilot projects to full-scale deployments, and the momentum behind the CR-9 and our follow-on roadmap puts Veridane in the middle of that transition. Bookings are weighted toward fiscal 2027 deliveries, and we are expanding capacity to serve them, prioritizing that investment within our capital spending plan and sizing it to the backlog we hold.

**Building Controls & Valves.** BCV net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% from $301.2 million a year ago, on softer commercial construction activity, cautious distributor ordering, and the temporary pause in new GV-400 orders from some OEM customers pending the recall notice. BCV backlog of $343.8 million was essentially level with a year ago, up 0.6%. We are managing what we can control in BCV: price and cost discipline, tight working capital, and the structural cost actions in Project Keystone, while the commercial construction cycle finds its footing.

On the GV-400 program: in September we announced a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves supplied to OEM customers for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters. This was a proactive, customer-first action taken with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, and the joint recall notice was published in October. We identified the root cause — an out-of-specification diaphragm material from a supplier lot — and corrective action is complete. Replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon, Wisconsin plant since September 28, and no injuries have been reported. In the third quarter we recorded a $21.6 million charge for the recall program, covering field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement, and logistics. We are working closely with the OEM customers who paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice, and their impact is reflected in the updated guidance below.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion, from $1.78–1.84 billion, and to adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million, from $255–270 million. The update reflects softer core commercial HVAC demand, the temporary GV-400 order pauses pending the recall notice, and the pace at which data-center shipments convert from our record backlog. TDC demand remains strong, and data-center bookings are weighted toward fiscal 2027 deliveries, which is where we expect the revenue inflection to build.

## Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders — quarter ended September 30, 2026

DRAFT — prepared by IR for review by Dana Whitcombe (CEO) and Mark Ostrander (CFO). For release with Q3 FY2026 results on Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET.

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center momentum is the story of our third quarter, and it is the engine that will carry Veridane forward. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) grew net sales 13.4% year over year, we won two new hyperscale platform awards, and our data-center backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. Total backlog ended the quarter at $918.0 million, up 13.0%, giving us visibility well into fiscal 2027. Growth is not evenly spread across our markets, but it is compounding where demand is strongest, and it is structural.

The quarter also reflected the challenges we have flagged to you: our core commercial HVAC business was soft, and our voluntary GV-400 valve recall weighed on results. Net sales were $412.6 million, adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, and adjusted EPS was $0.15. Reported results also include the recall and restructuring charges described below; the KPI table accompanying this letter presents the quarter's GAAP results in full, together with reconciliations of our non-GAAP measures. We moved fast on the recall, we have a clear and specific cost plan in Project Keystone, and we are updating our full-year guidance to reflect the demand environment we see.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale platform awards won in the quarter.
- Record data-center backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million and adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- Voluntary, proactive GV-400 recall completed with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) under its Fast Track program — root cause corrected, replacement valves shipping since September 28, and no injuries reported.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of run-rate cost savings by the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** TDC net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from $137.8 million a year ago, driven by sustained demand for our liquid-cooling portfolio across hyperscale and colocation customers. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger, launched in the second quarter with two hyperscale customers, continued to ramp, and the two new hyperscale platform awards won this quarter validate the roadmap we shared with you in August. TDC backlog finished the quarter at a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year, reflecting demand from both new and existing customers. Liquid cooling is moving from pilot projects to full-scale deployments, and the momentum behind the CR-9 and our follow-on roadmap puts Veridane in the middle of that transition. Bookings are weighted toward fiscal 2027 deliveries, and we are expanding capacity to serve them, prioritizing that investment within our capital spending plan and sizing it to the backlog we hold.

**Building Controls & Valves.** BCV net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% from $301.2 million a year ago, on softer commercial construction activity, cautious distributor ordering, and the temporary pause in new GV-400 orders from some OEM customers pending the recall notice. BCV backlog of $343.8 million was essentially level with a year ago, up 0.6%. We are managing what we can control in BCV: price and cost discipline, tight working capital, and the structural cost actions in Project Keystone, while the commercial construction cycle finds its footing.

On the GV-400 program: in September we announced a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves supplied to OEM customers for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters. This was a proactive, customer-first action taken with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, and the joint recall notice was published in October. We identified the root cause — an out-of-specification diaphragm material from a supplier lot — and corrective action is complete. Replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon, Wisconsin plant since September 28, and no injuries have been reported. In the third quarter we recorded a $21.6 million charge for the recall program, covering field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement, and logistics. We are working closely with the OEM customers who paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice, and their impact is reflected in the updated guidance below.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion, from $1.78–1.84 billion, and to adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million, from $255–270 million. The update reflects softer core commercial HVAC demand, the temporary GV-400 order pauses pending the recall notice, and the pace at which data-center shipments convert from our record backlog. TDC demand remains strong, and data-center bookings are weighted toward fiscal 2027 deliveries, which is where we expect the revenue inflection to build.

Cost actions are underway. Project Keystone targets approximately $35 million of run-rate cost savings by the second quarter of fiscal 2027, and we recorded a $6.2 million restructuring charge in the third quarter to initiate the program. With the recall charge behind us, Keystone savings, and richer TDC mix as data-center volumes ramp, we expect margins to recover through fiscal 2027. The investments we are making in data-center capacity are deliberate and demand-backed — funded only where the backlog supports them.

We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash, and we are managing working capital and capital spending closely as we convert backlog into revenue and realize Keystone savings.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees — the speed and professionalism of the recall response reflected the best of Veridane — and our customers, particularly the OEM partners who have worked alongside us on the GV-400 program. Our focus is on what we control: converting our record data-center backlog, restoring core margins through Project Keystone, and positioning Veridane for a strong fiscal 2027. Thank you for your continued trust and support.

Dana Whitcombe
President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander
EVP & Chief Financial Officer
